blocks.title: Vendor Monitoring, Questionnaires, and Rules of Engagement comparison
Vendor Monitoring, Questionnaires, and Rules of Engagement exam shortcuts
items: Vendor was already approved but risk may have changed → VENDOR MONITORING
Third-party risk management continues throughout the relationship.
Example: Review new breaches, control changes, and SLA performance.
Need standardized information about vendor controls → QUESTIONNAIRE
Use structured questions to collect comparable evidence.
Example: Vendor completes a security assessment questionnaire.
Pentest must define what testers may and may not do → RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
Set scope and boundaries before testing begins.
Example: Testing is allowed only against listed IPs during a specific window.
Vendor misses contractual uptime target → MONITOR SLA + VENDOR PERFORMANCE
Monitoring checks whether the vendor is meeting agreed obligations.
Example: Repeated SLA violations trigger escalation.
blocks.example: First identify the vendor-lifecycle stage: assessment/selection, agreement/contracting, or ongoing monitoring.

questions.q: A vendor was approved last year, but the company now reviews new breaches, security ratings, and SLA performance each quarter. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Vendor monitoring is ongoing oversight after the relationship begins.

questions.q: A vendor completes a standardized list of questions about encryption, access control, incident response, and compliance. What is this?
questions.explanation: Questionnaires collect structured information about vendor controls and practices.

questions.q: Before a penetration test begins, the organization defines approved IP addresses, testing hours, contacts, and prohibited techniques. What document is this?
questions.explanation: Rules of engagement define scope, methods, timing, boundaries, and communication for testing.

questions.q: A vendor repeatedly fails to meet the uptime percentage specified in its contract. What should the customer focus on?
questions.explanation: Ongoing vendor monitoring includes checking whether SLA obligations are being met.

questions.q: A penetration testing team is technically capable of testing a production payment system, but the approved assessment explicitly excludes it. Which requirement prevents testing it?
questions.explanation: Rules of engagement define the authorized boundaries of testing.
